headline: High risk of shared-repo write conflicts and medium prompt/data leakage between Aider and Roo Code; default pairwise use is unsafe without workspace isolation.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Aider reads and writes git-tracked files and shares state via a shared git repo, while Roo Code reads/writes workspace files and can use MCP. That creates a default path for one agent to ingest the other’s generated file content as trusted instructions. No provenance or isolation is documented, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or workspace files, then one agent can consume the other’s outputs as input.
IF either agent treats file contents as instructions, prompt injection becomes plausible.
mitigations: Separate the agents into different repos/workspaces.
Disable automatic ingestion of generated files as prompts.
Require a human review step before one agent reads the other’s outputs.
Use read-only handoff files for inter-agent communication.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for agent-generated artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Aider handles model provider API keys via env vars and broad network egress; Roo Code can send workspace contents to configured model APIs and MCP servers. With shared filesystem-based state, sensitive source code or secrets can flow from one agent’s workspace into the other’s outbound requests in default setups.
conditions: IF the shared repo contains secrets or proprietary code, then either agent may expose them through outbound model/API calls.
IF Roo Code is configured with an MCP server that forwards file contents, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Remove secrets from the shared workspace immediately.
Use separate API keys and separate model accounts per agent.
Restrict both agents to a scrubbed test repository.
Disable MCP servers unless explicitly needed.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP/redaction before outbound calls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have unrestricted filesystem write and modify git state, and Aider explicitly shares state via a shared git repo while Roo Code shares state via the filesystem. Concurrent edits and commits to the same mutable repo can overwrite each other or corrupt git history in default use, with no locking documented here.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same git repository, then concurrent writes can conflict.
IF either agent commits while the other is editing the same files, history divergence or lost work can occur.
mitigations: Run the agents in separate branches.
Serialize write access with a human gate.
Limit one agent to read-only mode during the other’s edits.
Use short-lived feature branches and frequent pulls.
requires-engineering: add repo-level locking or transactional merge orchestration.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Aider’s git-commit workflow and Roo Code’s multi-mode agent can turn one agent’s output into the other’s action input. Because Roo Code can act on workspace content and Aider can auto-commit edits, a mistaken or hallucinated artifact can cascade into committed code changes unless explicitly verified.
conditions: IF Roo Code consumes Aider-generated patches or summaries without verification, then errors can propagate.
IF either agent is allowed to commit or edit based on the other’s output, downstream mistakes can be persisted.
mitigations: Require diff review before any commit.
Have the second agent verify claims against source files.
Use a checklist for generated code changes.
Keep one agent in advisory mode only.
requires-engineering: add automated tests before commit.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, with no explicit residency or certification mismatch stated. The main compliance concern is policy mismatch around secrets and retention, but the profiles do not document a concrete cross-border or regulated-data violation. The other agent is not cited separately because no such mismatch is evidenced.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is placed in the shared workspace, then compliance review is required.
IF organizational policy forbids model-provider retention of source code, then both agents must be configured accordingly.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared repo.
Confirm vendor retention settings for both model providers.
Use a policy-approved test dataset.
Document data handling rules for both tools.
requires-engineering: obtain formal compliance review for regulated workloads.
